basis: Independent audiovisual model observation, not human listening or production approval

original_result.comparison_reason: First delivers a dynamic, richly illustrated treatment that fully complies with modern film standards, featuring varied camera setups (close-up hero framing, low-angle robot perspective, first-person handheld diagnostic view, and repair action with animated feedback). In contrast, Second repeats the exact failure mode warned against in MODERN_FILM.md: a single, virtually static frontal equipment tableau held across the entire runtime with crude blocky 3D primitives, an unconvincing workstation cart substituting for a handheld tool, and prolonged unrewarded holds exceeding 5 seconds.

first.one_viewing_summary: A polished, expressive editorial film that clearly tracks the Houston data center cooling unit incident using varied shot framings, distinct props (robot inspector, handheld thermal gun, wrench repair), and crisp infographic signposts.
observed_strengths: Excellent shot variety and framing transitions: tight crop on the overheating unit, dynamic low-angle framing on the inspection robot, first-person diagnostic view, and synthesis closing shot.
Finished visual assets with detailed texturing, clear contact, motivated lighting, and responsive UI overlays (checkmarks, temperature lines, flags).
Action-consequence grammar is explicit: thermal reading triggers inspection flag, handheld tool verifies measurement, wrench tightens hardware, and status returns to normal.
Clear adherence to source limits, explicitly stating the pilot status as ongoing and noting that the second unit's spike was unconfirmed as a fault.

defects.observed: The text card showing the September 23rd vendor update stays static slightly longer than needed before transitioning into the closing takeaway.

second.one_viewing_summary: A flat, repetitive 3D staging locked onto a single wide equipment view with basic primitive geometry, lack of shot variety, and awkward prop staging.
observed_strengths: Color-coded schematic temperature banding (pink vs. blue stripes) directly visualizes the heat difference between units.
Narration and audio mix are properly timed and aligned with source facts.

defects.observed: The camera never changes angle, framing, or focal depth; the entire piece is locked onto the same frontal equipment tableau, directly violating the modern film policy requiring at least three distinct framings.
Narration specifies a 'handheld check', but the scene stages a large wheeled computer terminal cart rolled in front of the unit, contradicting subject recognition and practical understanding.
A static cart sits in front of the units with negligible visible motion or reveal for over 9 seconds across the closing beats, violating the maximum reward interval and hold limits.
Cooling units, fans, and carts are built out of primitive polygonal shapes with flat shading, harsh untextured facets, and ungrounded contact shadows.

original_result.audio_observed: Both cuts share clean, balanced voiceover track and background underscore with clear caption alignment. First integrates subtle, effective visual-audio synchrony with snappy pops and confirmation cues.
original_result.source_limits: Both cuts respect source facts c1-c8: they attribute findings to vendor self-reports, distinguish the confirmed first condenser fault from the unconfirmed second unit spike, and clearly identify the pilot as ongoing as of the September 23rd update without inventing autonomous repairs.
